facts.statement: The fossil material was discovered by private collector L.-R. Hou in the Chiting Formation of Tainan City, Taiwan.
facts.quote: The Pavo miejue fossil material was discovered by L.-R. Hou, a private fossil collector, in outcrops of the Chiting Formation in Tainan City, Taiwan.

facts.statement: The morphology of Pavo miejue closely matches the genus Pavo, a group that does not currently occur in Taiwan.
Pavo miejue was significantly larger than modern galliform birds found in Taiwan, with a size comparable to large peafowls.
Pavo miejue extends the known distribution of the genus Pavo to easternmost Asia.
facts.quote: P. miejue is the first extinct bird recorded from Taiwan, as well as the first instance of an extinct Asian peafowl.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database currently has no specific record for Pavo miejue, only for the genus Pavo.
facts.quote: NOTE: PBDB has no record for Pavo miejue yet. This record describes its genus Pavo; nothing here is specific to Pavo miejue.
